summary: This is Part 14 of a detailed commentary on Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) by the late scholar Shams al-Din al-Dhahabi. Sheikh Ali Mashhour provides an in-depth explanation of the proper way to perform ruku (bowing) in prayer, emphasizing the spiritual meaning behind the physical posture as a manifestation of humility before Allah and exaltation of His greatness. The lecture covers the specific body positioning, the importance of maintaining a straight back, the prohibition of reciting Quran while bowing, and the transitions between ruku and standing. The speaker explains that the standing position after ruku should be of equal length to the ruku itself, during which believers recite "Sami allahu liman hamidah" followed by various duas. The lecture also discusses how some governors during the Umayyad period began shortening these positions, which was not the practice of the Prophet Muhammad or his companions.
